quote: She spoke with… pride? Self-satisfaction? A deliberate flaunting of herself
content: The datum is not her face. It is what she said: a cosmogonic myth delivered with a flourish, and then, unprompted, the observation that Vikings could not have had a cow because Scandinavia has no cows — an explicit disavowal of the content she had just recited. That is a report of speech and self-description, and Barrett’s work on the unreliability of reading discrete emotions from facial configurations does not bear on it. The essay’s conclusion is that some utterances function as displays rather than as assertions, and the evidence for it in this case is the speaker’s own commentary on her utterance.

quote: But even the concept of “religious profession” doesn’t seem to cover the pagan woman’s claim to believe in the primordial cow.
content: Luhrmann and Magliocco are describing the essay’s phenomenon, not refuting it. That practitioners hold myth as symbolic, aesthetic and identity-affirming and say so openly is what "cheering" names; the essay adds the observation that this is not merely a fourth kind of belief but a different speech act, which is a contribution the ethnographies do not make and do not contradict. Nor does the essay claim priority: it presents the category as one it needed and did not have. A taxonomy extended to fit the cases it meets is a taxonomy behaving correctly.

quote: most people are honest enough that, if they say a religious statement aloud, they will also feel obligated to say the verbal sentence into their own stream of consciousness
content: The statistic does not say what it is used for here. Hurlburt’s twenty-six percent is the proportion of sampled moments containing inner speech in daily life, not the proportion of people who use it, and nearly all of his subjects report inner speech at some rate; the tail of near-zero reporters is small and disputed. The essay’s claim concerns what happens when a person states a proposition aloud in a context that invites sincerity, which is a high-demand condition for inner verbalization, not a random moment of the day. And the essay is not equating belief with sentences: it is arguing that professing produces a sentence and that in most people the sentence drags a commitment behind it, which is why professing without belief takes work.
